title: UK house prices record steepest monthly fall since 2023
summary:
UK house prices fell 0.6% in October, the steepest monthly decline in more than three years, as elevated mortgage rates continue to weigh on market activity. The average property price stood at £296,285, marking the fourth consecutive monthly decline and the largest year-on-year fall since October 2023.

title: Rightmove lowers revenue forecasts as AI investment rises
summary:
Rightmove has downgraded its revenue growth forecasts for 2026 whilst announcing plans to accelerate its artificial intelligence development programme. The property portal now expects revenue growth of 6% to 7% for 2026, down from previous guidance of 6% to 8%.

title: Five inverted-layout homes on market across England
summary:
Five properties featuring inverted floor plans have been listed for sale across England, with prices ranging from £345,000 to £2 million. The properties, located in Kent, Buckinghamshire, Cornwall, Lancashire and Suffolk, demonstrate a design approach that places principal reception rooms on upper floors.

title: UK property sales hold steady despite market pessimism
summary:
The UK property market recorded 1.032 million sales subject to contract year-to-date, up 10.6% on 2023 despite negative sentiment. However, exchange rates remain concerning with just 49.2% of October listings completing, below the seven-year average of 57.6%.

title: Savills forecasts 1.5% house price fall for next year
summary:
Savills has forecast a 1.5% decline in UK house prices for next year, citing prolonged geopolitical tensions and persistently high mortgage rates as key factors. The estate agency expects mortgage rates to remain above 5% until early 2028, with a total peak-to-trough price decline of approximately 3%.

title: Winkworth names new director for Pimlico office
summary:
Estate agency Winkworth has appointed Lawrence Brown as Director of its Pimlico office, bringing over 20 years of UK property market experience to the role. Brown previously worked in the area for a decade and held senior positions at Chestertons and regional agencies.

title: Vistry to close 12 offices as debts reach £800m
summary:
Housebuilder Vistry is closing 12 of its 25 offices as part of a restructuring aimed at saving £50 million next year. The closures come as the company expects its debts to reach £800 million in the second half of 2027.

title: Scottish and North East towns dominate affordability rankings
summary:
Scotland and the North East of England account for 31 of the 36 most affordable towns in Britain, where typical home values remain below twice the combined annual earnings of two local full-time workers. The property portal's analysis of 929 towns found that a typical home is valued at £299,100, equivalent to 4.3 times annual household earnings.

title: Chester sales negotiator joins CAPP committee
summary:
Anna Horne, a sales negotiator at Chester estate agency Cavendish, has been appointed to the committee of the Chester Association of Property Professionals. She replaces David Adams, managing director of Cavendish, who served on the committee for 16 years.

title: Bank of England raises interest rates to 4% amid inflation concerns
summary:
The Bank of England has increased interest rates from 3.75% to 4%, marking the first rise in three years as policymakers seek to control inflation driven by rising fuel and energy costs. The Monetary Policy Committee voted unanimously to raise the Bank Rate after inflation climbed from 3.1% in August to 3.5% in September.
